question: Does real FA3 E4M3 attention change correct multiple-choice answers, including larger and other-family models?

hellaswag.sample: uniform without replacement, random.Random(seed), sorted source order

mmlu.sample: subject-stratified proportional largest-remainder allocation; deterministic subject-specific seed

selection_publication: All item IDs, source revisions and rendered prompts are committed before any GPU accuracy run.
special_tokens: Harness HFLM default add_bos_token=None: tokenizer-native default special tokens. Jointly encode context plus continuation; no chat template.

harness.normalization: ARC/HellaSwag divide continuation log-likelihood by rendered choice character length; MMLU unnormalized label log-likelihood

scoring.prediction: argmax standard task score; first index wins an exact tie
scoring.batching: same exact sequence length without padding, preserving full causal masking
scoring.projection: native BF16 vocabulary projection only at continuation prediction positions
scoring.reference: matched native GPU BF16 SDPA; no CPU or earlier loss baseline
scoring.maximum_length: model context limit; reject overlength rather than silently change an item

bootstrap.method: percentile interval of with-replacement item resampling; paired -1/0/+1 counts are sufficient and may be resampled multinomially

harm_rule.definition: variant accuracy minus BF16 <= -0.02 and the upper endpoint of its paired 95% interval < 0

interpretation: Report every model/task/variant. Intervals describe the fixed sampled task distributions, not a universal model-performance guarantee; multiple comparisons are not familywise corrected.

kernel.key_centering: FP64 mean/subtraction before FP32 Q/K rotation and native FP8 packing
kernel.rotated_operands: Q and K only; V unchanged

new_model_risk_forecasts: Not computed: accuracy transfer is primary; no retrospective predictor fitting.
batch_limit: Full-sequence quantization scales and key means can use later tokens; these are batch multiple-choice scores, not streaming generation.
